source_text: τὸν οὐχ ὁλοκλήρως εἰς ἔργα χωρεῖν δυνάμενον, οὔτε μὴν ἀδιάβλητον ἔχοντα παντελῶς τὴν βάδισιν, ἤτοι τὴν ἐνέργειαν, τὴν ὡς ἐν πολιτείᾳ, φημὶ, καὶ ζωῇ τῇ ἐννομωτάτῃ. Εἶεν δ' ἂν καὶ οὗτοι πάλιν, ἢ οἱ ποιοῦντες τὸ ἔργον Κυρίου ἀμελῶς, οἷς ἐπενήνεκται τὸ οὐαὶ διὰ προφήτου φωνῆς, ἤγουν οἱ τὸ δίκαιον οὐ δικαίως διώκοντες, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Ἐπιτήρει δὲ ὅτι τῇ νοητῇ καὶ ὁλοτελεῖ χωλότητι, καὶ ἡ μετρία τοῦ σκέλους πήρωσις ἐν ἴσῳ τέ ἐστι, καὶ ὡς ταὐτὸν λελόγισται. Τῷ γὰρ μηδ' ὅλως τι δρᾷν ἰσχύσαι τῶν ἀγαθῶν, τὸ μὴ δρᾷν ὀρθῶς ἐν ἴσῳ κείσεται λόγῳ. Φαίνοιτο δ' ἂν εἰκότως ἐν μὲν τῇ χωλότητι, τὸ μηδ' ὅλως· ἐν δὲ τῷ συντρίμματι, τὸ μὴ ὑγιῶς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἔοικε. {ΚΥΡ.} Κυρτὸν δὲ, καὶ ἔφηλον, καὶ πτιλὸν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καταγράφει πάλιν ὡς ἐν τοῖς ἀδοκιμωτάτοις. Καὶ κυρτὸν μὲν εἶναί φαμεν, τὸν οἱονεὶ κεκυφότα, καὶ κάτω βλέποντα νῷ, καὶ πρὸς τὰ σαρκὸς νενευκότα πάθη, καὶ τοῖς ἐπιγείοις τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν ἐπερείδοντα, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τὸν νοητὸν, καὶ εἰς τοῦτο γνώμης ἰόντα λοιπὸν, ὡς τὸ ἀπορθοῦσθαι μισεῖν, πρός γέ φημι τὸ χρῆναι τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖν. Εἶεν δ' ἂν ἐν τούτοις τὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐγκλήματα, περὶ ὧν γέγραπται· «Σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.» Ἔφηλον δὲ, τὸν τὴν ἐφηλίδα τὴν καλουμένην ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἔχοντα μετώποις. Ἀῤῥώστημα δὲ τουτὶ καταμελαίνειν εἶδος τὴν ἐπ' ἄκρου δέρματος ὄψιν. Παραιρεῖται δὲ τοῖς οἷς ἂν γένοιτο παθεῖν, τὸ κἂν γοῦν ἰσχύσαι λαθεῖν, αὐταῖς ἐπανθοῦν ὀφρύσιν, ὅλοις τε προσώποις ἐπηρτημένον. Ἔφηλος δὴ οὖν ὁ τοιόσδε σωματικῶς, νοητῶς γε μὴν ὑποφαίνει τὸν ἀσχήμονα, γυμνῶς τε καὶ ἀκρύπτως, καὶ οἱονεὶ πρόσωπον οὐκ ἔχοντα καθαρὸν, ἀλλ' ἐκφανὲς ἅπασι τὸ ἀκαλλὲς εἰς ζωὴν, ὡς μὴ εἰδέναι που τάχα, μηδὲ τὸ ὑπό του τῶν σοφῶν ὀρθῶς εἰρημένον, «Σοφοὶ κρύψουσι τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς ἔφης; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐ γὰρ, ὦ Παλλάδιε, μυρία ὅσα γε τὰ ἐν ἡμῖν ἐστι πάθη; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ναί· τί οὖν τοῦτό γε; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὅτι, ὦ γενναῖε, φημὶ, νοσεῖ μὲν ἕκαστος, ἃ νοσεῖ, αἰδοῖ δὲ πολλάκις τῇ πρὸς ἀδελφοὺς ἡττώμενος, ἐν σπουδῇ καὶ λόγῳ ποιεῖται πολλῷ καὶ τὸ ἐῤῥῶσθαι δοκεῖν, καὶ τὸ λανθάνειν ἐν κακοῖς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ λέγεις. {ΚΥΡ.} Εἰ δὲ δή τις εἴη πρὸς τοῦτο ἥκων ἀναισχυντίας, ὡς ἡγεῖσθαι παρ' οὐδὲν, τὸ καὶ ἐκφανδὸν ἑλέσθαι πλημμελεῖν, καὶ τῶν εἰς κοσμιότητα γερῶν ἀφειδῆσαι παντελῶς, οὐκ ἄν τῳ δόξειεν ὁ τοιόσδε λοιπὸν, τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ ἁγίου γένους οἴχεσθαι μακράν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔφηλον τοίνυν ὁ νόμος ἀποκαλεῖ τὸν τοιοῦτον, ὡς οὐδὲ κρύπτειν εἰδότα καὶ ἀνεχόμενον τὸ συμβὰν ἀῤῥώστημα καὶ πάθος αὐτῷ. Πτιλὸν δὲ τοὺς
pass_a_gloss: [cont. Lev 21:19 crushed foot/hand] 'the one not able wholly to go into works', unblameable walk activity, conduct most lawful life. These = carelessly, on whom the woe was brought by the prophet's voice; or 'pursuing the just not justly', as written. 'observe': to spiritual and complete lameness the moderate maiming of the leg is equal, reckoned the same. Not being able to do any good at all = not doing rightly. Lameness shows 'not at all'; the crushing 'not soundly'. PALL: 'it seems'. CYR: hunchback, ἔφηλος (blotched, with ἐφηλίς), bleary/lashless eyed listed again among the most unapproved. κυρτός = 'bent over', 'looking down in mind', 'inclined to flesh's passions', 'fixing eye on earthly' (the νοητὸν eye), going so far in 'mind set' as 'to hate being straightened', toward 'thinking things above'. Here charges; quote σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ... 'bend down their back always'. having the ἐφηλίς on the forehead; ailment 'blackening' the surface skin look; 'takes away' even 'escaping notice', 'blooming on brows', 'spread over' whole faces. Spiritually the unseemly 'nakedly and unhidden', 'ugliness in life plain to all', not knowing what one of the wise said: 'the wise will hide their shames'. PALL: 'how do you mean'. CYR: not countless passions in us? PALL: ναί, so what? CYR: ὦ γενναῖε, each 'is sick with what he is sick', but αἰδοῖ ... 'overcome by shame' before brothers, takes much effort and account both 'to seem healthy' and 'to escape notice in evils'. PALL: εὖ λέγεις. CYR: if someone comes to such shamelessness as to count as nothing 'choosing openly to sin', and 'to disregard the honours of decency' entirely, would he not seem 'gone far from the sacred and holy race'? PALL: καὶ μάλα. CYR: the law calls such a one ἔφηλος, as not knowing nor enduring to hide the ἀῤῥώστημα καὶ πάθος. πτιλὸν δὲ τοὺς [ὀφθαλμούς continues in 6].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the one who cannot carry his deeds through to the full, and whose walk, that is, his activity, is not entirely beyond reproach: I mean in conduct and in a life lived fully by the law. These again would be those who do the work of the Lord carelessly, against whom the voice of the prophet has pronounced woe (Jeremiah 48:10), or those who pursue what is just, but not justly, as it is written (Deuteronomy 16:20). Notice that even a moderate injury to the leg is put on the same level as spiritual and complete lameness, and is counted as the same thing. For not doing good rightly will be placed on the same footing as being unable to do any good at all. One may fairly see in lameness the ‘not at all,’ and in the crushed limb the ‘not soundly.’

Cyril: Again, he lists the hunchback, the man with blotches, and the man with bleary eyes among the most unfit (Leviticus 21:20). We say the hunchback is the one who is, as it were, bent over: he looks downward in mind, leans toward the passions of the flesh, and fixes his eye on earthly things (clearly, the eye of the mind), and has at last come to such a frame of mind that he hates to be set upright, I mean, for the duty of setting the mind on things above (Colossians 3:2). Under this would fall the charges against the Jews, of whom it is written: ‘Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see, and bend their back for ever’ (Psalm 69:23; Romans 11:10). The man with blotches is one who has what is called a blotch on his very forehead. This is a kind of sickness that darkens the surface of the skin. It takes from those who suffer it even the chance of staying hidden, since it breaks out on the very brows and spreads over the whole face. Such a man, then, is blotched in body; but in a spiritual sense he points to the man who is unseemly openly and without concealment, who has, as it were, no clean face, but whose ugliness of life is plain to all, so that perhaps he does not even know what one of the wise rightly said: ‘The wise will hide their own shames.’
Cyril: Are there not, Palladius, countless passions in us?

Cyril: This, my good friend: each of us is sick with his own sickness, but often, overcome by shame before his brothers, he takes great pains and care both to seem healthy and to keep his faults out of sight.

Cyril: But suppose someone has come to such shamelessness that he thinks nothing of choosing to sin openly and of throwing away entirely the honors that belong to a decent life. Would not anyone think that such a man has gone far from the sacred and holy race?

choices.why: 'The wise will hide their own shames' is introduced as 'one of the wise' and has no exact LXX match (Proverbs 10:14 LXX begins 'σοφοὶ κρύψουσιν αἴσθησιν', 'the wise will hide discernment'); left uncited.

Lev 21:20 terms: κυρτός hunchback; ἔφηλος, which Cyril explains as a dark blotch (ἐφηλίς) on the forehead and face (LXX sense is probably a white speck in the eye, but his reading governs), rendered 'with blotches'; πτίλος τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, eyes that have lost their lashes, rendered 'bleary eyes' to fit his reading in section 6 (sees, but not soundly).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence, continuing Leviticus 21:19 (crushed foot or hand) from section 4. Jeremiah 48:10 = LXX Jeremiah 31:10, which reads 'cursed (ἐπικατάρατος) is he who does the works of the Lord carelessly'; Cyril calls it 'the woe' (τὸ οὐαί), so 'woe' is kept as his word. 'Pursue what is just, but not justly' inverts LXX Deuteronomy 16:20 'δικαίως τὸ δίκαιον διώξῃ' (justly pursue what is just). Psalm 69:23 = LXX Psalm 68:24; the same wording is quoted at Romans 11:10, and Cyril's framing (charges against the Jews) echoes Paul. 'Setting the mind on things above' (τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖν) is Colossians 3:2. 'The wise will hide their own shames' is introduced as 'one of the wise' and has no exact LXX match (Proverbs 10:14 LXX begins 'σοφοὶ κρύψουσιν αἴσθησιν', 'the wise will hide discernment'); left uncited. The old English's '(Sirach 20:26?)' was dropped. Lev 21:20 terms: κυρτός hunchback; ἔφηλος, which Cyril explains as a dark blotch (ἐφηλίς) on the forehead and face (LXX sense is probably a white speck in the eye, but his reading governs), rendered 'with blotches'; πτίλος τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, eyes that have lost their lashes, rendered 'bleary eyes' to fit his reading in section 6 (sees, but not soundly). The paragraph ends mid-phrase ('Πτιλὸν δὲ τοὺς | ὀφθαλμούς'); section 6 opens '…eyes'.

Lev 21:19 crushed foot/hand] τὸν οὐχ ὁλοκλήρως εἰς ἔργα χωρεῖν δυνάμενον 'the one not able wholly to go into works', οὔτε ἀδιάβλητον (unblameable) ἔχοντα τὴν βάδισιν (walk) ἤτοι τὴν ἐνέργειαν (activity), ἐν πολιτείᾳ (conduct) καὶ ζωῇ τῇ ἐννομωτάτῃ (most lawful life). These = οἱ ποιοῦντες τὸ ἔργον Κυρίου ἀμελῶς (carelessly), on whom τὸ οὐαί (the woe) was brought by the prophet's voice; or οἱ τὸ δίκαιον οὐ δικαίως διώκοντες 'pursuing the just not justly', as written. ἐπιτήρει 'observe': to νοητῇ καὶ ὁλοτελεῖ χωλότητι (spiritual and complete lameness) the μετρία τοῦ σκέλους πήρωσις (moderate maiming of the leg) is ἐν ἴσῳ (equal), reckoned the same. Not being able to do any good at all (μηδ' ὅλως δρᾶν) = not doing rightly (μὴ δρᾶν ὀρθῶς). Lameness shows τὸ μηδ' ὅλως 'not at all'; the σύντριμμα (crushing) τὸ μὴ ὑγιῶς 'not soundly'. PALL: ἔοικε 'it seems'. CYR: κυρτός (hunchback), ἔφηλος (blotched, with ἐφηλίς), πτιλὸς τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς (bleary/lashless-eyed) listed again among the ἀδοκιμώτατοι (most unapproved). κυρτός = κεκυφώς 'bent over', κάτω βλέπων νῷ 'looking down in mind', νενευκὼς πρὸς τὰ σαρκὸς πάθη 'inclined to flesh's passions', ἐπερείδων τὸν ὀφθαλμὸν τοῖς ἐπιγείοις 'fixing eye on earthly' (the νοητὸν eye), going so far in γνώμη 'mind-set' as τὸ ἀπορθοῦσθαι μισεῖν 'to hate being straightened', toward τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖν 'thinking things above'. Here τὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐγκλήματα (charges); quote σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ... τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον 'bend down their back always'. ἔφηλος = having the ἐφηλίς on the forehead (μέτωπον); ἀῤῥώστημα (ailment) καταμελαίνειν 'blackening' the surface skin look; παραιρεῖται 'takes away' even τὸ λαθεῖν 'escaping notice', ἐπανθοῦν ὀφρύσιν 'blooming on brows', ἐπηρτημένον 'spread over' whole faces. Spiritually ὑποφαίνει τὸν ἀσχήμονα (the unseemly) γυμνῶς τε καὶ ἀκρύπτως 'nakedly and unhidden', πρόσωπον οὐκ ἔχοντα καθαρόν, ἐκφανὲς ἅπασι τὸ ἀκαλλὲς εἰς ζωήν 'ugliness in life plain to all', not knowing what one of the wise said: σοφοὶ κρύψουσι τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας 'the wise will hide their shames'. PALL: πῶς ἔφης 'how do you mean'. CYR: not μυρία πάθη (countless passions) in us? PALL: ναί, so what? CYR: ὦ γενναῖε, each νοσεῖ ἃ νοσεῖ 'is sick with what he is sick', but αἰδοῖ ... ἡττώμενος 'overcome by shame' before brothers, takes much σπουδή καὶ λόγος (effort and account) both τὸ ἐῤῥῶσθαι δοκεῖν 'to seem healthy' and τὸ λανθάνειν ἐν κακοῖς 'to escape notice in evils'. PALL: εὖ λέγεις. CYR: if someone comes to such ἀναισχυντία (shamelessness) as to count as nothing ἐκφανδὸν ἑλέσθαι πλημμελεῖν 'choosing openly to sin', and τῶν εἰς κοσμιότητα γερῶν ἀφειδῆσαι 'to disregard the honours of decency' entirely, would he not seem τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ ἁγίου γένους οἴχεσθαι μακράν 'gone far from the sacred and holy race'? PALL: καὶ μάλα. CYR: the law calls such a one ἔφηλος, as not knowing (εἰδότα) nor enduring (ἀνεχόμενον) to hide (κρύπτειν) the ἀῤῥώστημα καὶ πάθος. πτιλὸν δὲ τοὺς [ὀφθαλμούς continues in 6].
